about: Priorities of donor families reported by others: news outlets, a league voter guide and city records. Each is kept apart from priorities in a donor's own words (data/priorities.json): the words are the reporter's or a third party's unless 'speaker' says a named person of the donor is quoted. 'read' says whether the page was read in full or only a search-result extract of it; collect_pages.py re-fetches each page and records in data/reported_check.json whether the quote is on it. 'suggests' is a reading of what priority the source points to, not a statement by the donor.

entries.outlet: City and County of San Francisco, Department of Elections (sf.gov)
entries.read: search-result extract of the page read; page not read in full
entries.speaker: The city's list of qualified measures, under 'D - Changes to Ballot Measure Process'
entries.quote: Official Opponent Argument Author: San Francisco Labor Council
entries.suggests: Opposes Prop D; the Council wrote the official opposing argument in the voter pamphlet.
entries.caveat: The page lists the author only; the argument itself (a PDF linked from the page) was not read.

entries.read: search-result extract of the page read; page not read in full
entries.speaker: Reporter's statement of fact
entries.quote: The council also contributed $20,000 against the measure.
entries.suggests: Opposes Prop D and put money behind that position (the sentence before it, in the same article, says its Committee on Political Education voted to oppose the measure).
entries.caveat: The $20,000 is outside spending or a gift to a measure committee, not a gift to any official's committee.

entries.read: search-result extract of the page read; page not read in full
entries.speaker: Kim Tavaglione, executive director of the San Francisco Labor Council, quoted
entries.quote: Quadrupling is never a good thing
entries.suggests: Opposes the quadrupling of the signature requirement in Prop D.
entries.caveat: In a newspaper's endorsement editorial; the words are the executive director's, the framing is the editorial's.

entries.read: page read in full
entries.speaker: Bianca Polovina, president of IFPTE Local 21, quoted
entries.quote: If we don't have things like clean streets, strong hospitals, and effective transit, we don't have a recovery
entries.suggests: Priority: city services and city jobs; opposes the Mayor's proposed layoffs.
entries.caveat: Said in April 2026 about layoffs, not about a ballot measure.

entries.read: page read in full
entries.speaker: Bianca Polovina, president of IFPTE Local 21, quoted
entries.quote: When we talk about cutting essential services, cutting jobs, this is a choice, it is not a necessity.
entries.suggests: Priority: keeping city jobs and services funded rather than cut.
entries.caveat: Same article and speaker as IFPTE-RECOVERY.

entries.read: search-result extract of the page read; page not read in full
entries.speaker: Reporter's statement of what the union argues
entries.quote: The union argues Lurie is trying to privatize work that should be done by city staff
entries.suggests: Priority: city staff, not contractors, doing permitting work; objects to the Mayor's plan.
entries.caveat: Reporter's summary of the union's formal objection; the objection itself was not read.

entries.read: page read in full
entries.speaker: Reporter's statement of fact
entries.quote: The San Francisco Building and Construction Trades Council and Laborers Local 261 recommended removing "affordable housing" last week.
entries.suggests: Took a position on how the Prop I digest describes the measure (asked that 'affordable housing' be removed from it); a position on wording, not on Prop I itself.
entries.caveat: The article links a letter to the Ballot Simplification Council; the letter was not read.

entries.outlet: Office of the Mayor, press release on sf.gov
entries.read: search-result extract of the page read; page not read in full
entries.speaker: The Mayor's office, naming the coalition behind the BUILD Act
entries.quote: labor and business groups-including the San Francisco Building and Construction Trades Council, the North Coast States Carpenters Union, Laborers Union Local 261
entries.suggests: Backs the BUILD Act (housing construction and union jobs), which Mayor Lurie and Supervisor Mahmood introduced.
entries.caveat: The Mayor's own release names the groups; whether each one said so itself was not checked.

entries.read: search-result extract of the page read; page not read in full
entries.speaker: The Mayor's claim, reported by the paper
entries.quote: including from the San Francisco Building Construction and Trades Council, LiUNA Local 261, Teamsters 665, Teamsters 350 and Operating Engineers Local 3
entries.suggests: Reported to support Props D, E and F, on the Mayor's say-so.
entries.caveat: This is the Mayor's claim of who supports his measures, not the unions' own statement.

entries.read: page read in full
entries.speaker: Reporter's statement of fact
entries.quote: Jobs and her organization have long supported Lurie: Emerson gave $50,000 to the mayor's transition
entries.suggests: A record of support for Mayor Lurie, including his charter measures; no statement of what Emerson wants from them.
entries.caveat: Emerson Collective is a donor to Mission Local, which the article discloses. This reports a pattern of giving, not a priority in Emerson's words.

entries.read: page read in full
entries.speaker: Reporter's statement of fact, citing an SF Standard report
entries.quote: Lurie and Jobs have reportedly met to discuss a "branding campaign" for San Francisco
entries.suggests: A shared interest with the Mayor in the city's image (reported meeting).
entries.caveat: Same article and disclosure as EMERSON-LONG; the SF Standard report it links to was not read in full.

entries.quote: Firefighters Local 798, Transit Workers Union 250A, Teamsters Local 665, Chinatown TRIP

entries.caveat: The extract does not show which measure the list belongs to (my reading: a transit measure, Prop H, since Chinatown TRIP is a transit group) (unverified). A list of supporters, not the union's words.
